breakdown.title: How this Build Plan is calculated
breakdown.intro: Live {{hub}} prices and this plan's own inputs. Every number below is the one the plan is using now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsSell: Materials: {{hub}} lowest sell — what you pay to buy them now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsBuy: Materials: {{hub}} highest buy — what they cost if you place orders and wait.
breakdown.pricesOre: Ore, ice and gas: priced as themselves. Refining is not modelled, so a plan that eats minerals prices minerals.
breakdown.pricesOwned: Owned units: 0 ISK. Ore you mined is free here — the plan does not charge what you could have sold it for.
breakdown.pricesBuilt: Built materials: their own recipe instead of a price — inputs plus job fee, at every level you chose to build.
breakdown.pricesProduct: {{product}}: always {{hub}} lowest sell, whichever side the materials use.
breakdown.materials: Quantity after ME {{me}} waste (rounded once per job, not per run) × unit price. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.materialsReaction: Quantity × unit price. Reactions have no ME, so no waste is saved. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.jobFee: EIV is CCP's reference value for the materials at ME 0 — a yardstick, not what you pay. {{system}}'s index ({{index}}) scales it, SCC adds 4%, the structure owner adds tax.
breakdown.jobFeeFormula: EIV {{eiv}} → cost index fee {{costIndexFee}} + SCC 4% {{scc}} + facility tax {{facilityTax}} = {{total}}
breakdown.revenueTitle: Revenue, sales tax and broker fee
breakdown.revenueAssumption: Assumes it fills at today's lowest sell. Undercutting, price moves and time on the market are not modelled.
breakdown.fees: From your skills: Accounting {{accounting}} sets sales tax, Broker Relations {{broker}} sets broker fee. Standings assumed 0.
breakdown.profitNet: Net = revenue − sales tax − broker fee − total cost. The default.
breakdown.profitGross: Gross = revenue − total cost. Ignores both market fees — only realistic if you never list it.
breakdown.profitIskPerHour: ISK/hour = profit ÷ build time ({{time}}). Slot time, not time to sell.
breakdown.breakEven: What one unit must list at to cover the whole job. Fees come out of the listed price, so it sits above cost per unit.
breakdown.breakEvenFloor: Broker fee has a 100 ISK per-order minimum. Under that, 100 ISK is used and the price re-solved.
breakdown.verdictAcquisition: Acquisition: is building {{product}} cheaper than buying it? Nothing is sold, so no tax and no broker fee.
breakdown.verdictSale: Sale profitability: does building then selling make money? That one pays both fees. Same hub price, different question.
breakdown.useOrSellBody: Owned units cost the plan nothing, so the profit above is what you make on top of stock you already hold. Build if that beats what the materials would fetch, sell if it does not.
breakdown.useOrSellBases: Sell now: fills standing buy orders — paid at once, sales tax only. Sell order: lists at the hub's sell price — more ISK, but broker fee (100 ISK minimum) and you wait.
breakdown.useOrSellUnpriced: No order on the chosen side means no verdict, rather than a total that quietly drops it.
breakdown.useOrSellScope: Only the owned units this job eats are valued. Surplus is out of scope, and a material set to Built counts as itself, not as the stock behind its recipe.

orders.question: Which of my orders is quietly losing ISK?
orders.answer: Open Orders is a worklist, not a list. Every order is filed under the worst thing wrong with it — undercut at your station, system or region, sitting under the price where relisting stops paying, or about to expire — worst first, across every character you fly. Open one and it prices the ways out: hold, match the station, dump into a standing buy order, or refine it and sell the materials, each net of the fee that exit actually pays, plus the hubs bidding more and how many jumps away they are.

build.question: Is this blueprint worth building today?
build.answer: A Build Plan costs the materials, job fee and taxes at live hub prices and answers two different questions instead of blurring them: is it cheaper than buying outright, and does it still profit once sales tax and broker fees come off. Sub-builds recurse into the same plan, owned stock is checked against what it would fetch if you sold it instead, and every figure on screen opens the rule it came from with your own values substituted in.

training.question: What is this training plan really going to cost me?
training.answer: Drag skills into a plan and it schedules against the character's real attributes, implants and queue. The optimizer places remaps for you — or at markers you drop yourself — and re-costs the plan under what-if implants and an accelerator before you spend anything. Put your characters side by side to see which of them should be training it.

moon.question: Who owes what on the moon rental?
moon.answer: Your mining ledger becomes an invoice. Each day's ore in each system is assigned to a payee at a tax rate snapshotted on the spot, so a later price move never rewrites what was owed. If ESI reports more ore for a day you already assigned, it flags itself for review with the before and after. Then settle up against the donations and contracts you actually sent.

login.trustHeading: Read-only, and it stays that way

readOnly.name: It never writes to your account
readOnly.desc: No order is placed, no colony is touched, and nothing else about your mail is changed.

token.name: Your refresh token stays in this browser
token.desc: It lives in this browser's own storage and nowhere else — never on a server, never in a log. Signing in to sync exchanges one short-lived access token and never the refresh token. Remove a character and it goes with it.

offline.name: Works when the connection doesn't
offline.desc: Install it like an app. It keeps serving what it last fetched when ESI is down or you have no signal, and syncs your own plans across your devices.

openSource.name: Free, and open to read
openSource.desc: No account to create, no ads, no subscription, no paid tier. Read the source before you decide to trust it.

piPlan.spaceHint: Sets the starting customs rate only. It never changes yield — per-planet richness is scanner-only and is not in ESI.
piPlan.customsRateReset: Use the default for this space
piPlan.rateFromHighsecSkill: 10% highsec NPC base, less 1% per level of Customs Code Expertise — this character has level {{level}}. Any POCO owner tax is on top; edit the rate to add it.
piPlan.rateFromHighsecUnknown: 10% highsec NPC base, untrained. This character's skills haven't loaded, so Customs Code Expertise could not be applied — edit the rate if it is trained.
piPlan.rateFromPlayerPoco: Outside highsec a player POCO has no NPC component, so Customs Code Expertise does nothing and this starts at 0%. Set the owner's tax yourself.
piPlan.rateEdited: Your own rate. Reset it to go back to the default for this space.
piPlan.layoutHint: Customs is charged where goods cross a planet boundary, not where they change tier. Two tiers made on one planet pay nothing between them, which is why the layout can flip the sign of the margin.
piPlan.floorHint: What you buy off the market; everything above it you make. Buying P1 needs no extractors at all, so it is fully answerable with no colonies.
piPlan.customsBetweenTooltip: Both sides of every hop the layout puts a planet boundary on — export off one planet and import onto the next. Zero when every made tier shares a planet.
piPlan.totalCostTooltip: Bought inputs plus customs. It excludes what the chain cannot see: no POCO fuel, no hauling and no time.
piPlan.footprintTooltip_one: You can run {{count}} planet at once, and one planet holds only so many pins. Planets, not ISK, are what runs out first — a floor that wins on margin while needing a colony you cannot build has not won.
piPlan.footprintTooltip_other: You can run {{count}} planets at once, and one planet holds only so many pins. Planets, not ISK, are what runs out first — a floor that wins on margin while needing a colony you cannot build has not won.
piPlan.footprintTooltipUnknown: How many planets you can run depends on your Interplanetary Consolidation level, which has not loaded yet. One planet holds only so many pins. Planets, not ISK, are what runs out first — a floor that wins on margin while needing a colony you cannot build has not won.
piPlan.p0MarketNote: P0 you extract is valued at the hub, not at zero: extracting it costs a planet slot and forgoes a sale. The P0 floor's edge is the processing margin and customs it avoids, not free inputs.
piPlan.needsRateHint: Supplying your own P0 depends on a planet you may not have, and there is no published yield per planet. Enter what one extractor program sustains per hour and this floor is costed; leave it blank and it stays unanswered rather than guessed at zero.
piPlan.notPriceableTitle: No verdict: not priceable at this hub
piPlan.notPriceableHint: {{hub}} has no sell order for {{names}}. Without a price there is no honest margin, so none is shown.
piPlan.pricesFailedTitle: Hub prices could not be fetched
piPlan.pricesFailedHint: The planner needs live market prices. Check your connection, then refresh.
piPlan.loadFailedHint: Planetary schematics or market prices failed to load. Refresh to try again.
piPlan.readTooltip: What the hub says about this tier on its own: whether processing it is worth more than its inputs cost. Before customs, and independent of the floor you picked — the customs rate is what can flip the whole chain.
piPlan.sensitivityTitle: Margin by sourcing floor and customs rate
piPlan.sensitivityTableLabel: Margin per unit for each sourcing floor across customs rates
piPlan.sensitivityHint: Which floor wins is a function of the rate, not a fixed answer: at 0% supplying your own P0 wins, and from 10% up buying P1 does.
piPlan.planetsTaxedTooltip: How many planet boundaries the layout puts inside the chain. It is what the customs bill is charged over, not how many planets the whole operation occupies.
piPlan.outputRequiredHint: The plan is sized from how many units a day you want. Give it a positive number and the verdict comes back.

piAdvisor.slotsTooltip: One colony per level of Interplanetary Consolidation, plus the one every capsuleer starts with. Counted across every system you have a colony in, not just this one.
piAdvisor.slotsAssumedTooltip: No skill data for this character yet, so Interplanetary Consolidation is assumed untrained — one colony. Every trained level adds another.
piAdvisor.noSlotFree: No colony slot free: you are running {{used}} of {{total}}. Train Interplanetary Consolidation to level {{level}} for another, or abandon a colony.
piAdvisor.noSlotFreeMax: No colony slot free: you are running all {{total}} colonies a capsuleer can have. Abandon one to build here.
piAdvisor.noMeasuredExtraction: No extractor here reports a complete program, so this colony has no measured rate.
piAdvisor.upgradeAvailable: Command Center at level {{level}}, and your skill allows {{max}}: the next level adds {{cpu}} tf and {{powergrid}} MW.
piAdvisor.networkHint: What all your colonies could make between them, across every system you have one in — not just the system shown below. Each card answers for its own planet alone, so a product needing two planets’ output can only be named here.
piAdvisor.networkTotal: +{{isk}} an hour over selling every P1 raw, at {{hub}} prices and this system’s {{percent}}% customs rate.
piAdvisor.networkTotalMixedRates: +{{isk}} an hour over selling every P1 raw, at {{hub}} prices — each priced at its own host's customs rate.
piAdvisor.networkGreedy: Allocated best-paying first — not provably optimal.
piAdvisor.networkAssumesRemoval: Assumes the unfed factories below come out first; this spends the budget they free up.
piAdvisor.networkNothing: Nothing yet: no two of these colonies make a pair of inputs that combine.

piAdvisor.altColoniesHint: Route between every character you have logged in, not just this one. Reads what is already cached, so a character whose colonies you have never opened will not appear.
piAdvisor.altColoniesCount_one: {{count}} colony from your other characters is in the plan.
piAdvisor.altColoniesCount_other: {{count}} colonies from your other characters are in the plan.
piAdvisor.buyInputsHint: The hub you can actually reach. Picking one lets the Advisor plan a purchase to feed a factory, and prices every figure on this tab at that market. None still routes between your own colonies — it only refuses to assume a shop.
piAdvisor.buyInputsOffNote: No hub picked, so only what your own colonies make is on the table. {{names}} would also be reachable by hauling inputs in.
piAdvisor.actionExtractFits: Add {{units}}x Extractor Control Unit and {{heads}} heads — +{{extra}}/hr of {{name}}, which feeds {{fed}} of the {{idle}} idle facilities.
piAdvisor.actionExtractOrRemove: Or feed them instead: once {{count}} come out there is room for an Extractor Control Unit and {{heads}} heads (+{{extra}}/hr of {{name}}), enough for {{fed}} of them. The same Powergrid cannot hold both.
piAdvisor.actionExtractNoRoom: Feeding them is not an option here: an Extractor Control Unit is {{cpu}} tf / {{powergrid}} MW before a single head, and even with all {{count}} removed this colony would have only {{free}} MW.
piAdvisor.actionExtractWanted: Closing the gap outright would take {{heads}} heads.
piAdvisor.actionAssumesRemoval: This assumes the idle facilities above come out first — the budget they are holding is where these go.
piAdvisor.actionConvertWhy: Nothing in your colonies uses that {{from}}, so those {{count}} are worth {{lost}} an hour selling it. The replacement clears {{gained}}.
piAdvisor.actionConvertHaul: You would be hauling {{in}} units an hour in and {{out}} units an hour out.
piAdvisor.actionAddEcon: Sells {{units}}/hr for {{revenue}}. Nothing to buy — you already make the inputs, and giving up their sale is what the margin is net of: +{{margin}} an hour after customs.
piAdvisor.actionAddEconBuy: Sells {{units}}/hr for {{revenue}}, against {{spend}} an hour of inputs you have to buy. +{{margin}} an hour after customs and the material you already make.
piAdvisor.actionNothing: Nothing to change here: every facility is fed, and no product your other colonies could feed was placed on this planet.

piAdvisor.capacityFootnoteNoLink: {{cpu}} tf and {{powergrid}} MW free as it stands.

piAdvisor.measuredOnlyHint: Measured where it can be: pins and extraction rates come from ESI, and each rate is the whole program averaged over its decay curve rather than its opening cycle. Extractor headroom assumes a full ten heads. A build recommendation is a projection from those measurements, and an unbuilt planet’s value is an estimate — both say so where they appear.

piAdvisor.cadenceRestartHint: Extractor output falls the longer a program runs, so reinstalling it puts you back at the top of the curve. This sets the program length, and with it how much comes out of the ground. Nothing on ESI answers it — it is a habit, so the Advisor asks.
piAdvisor.cadenceHaulLabel: I haul from the planet every
piAdvisor.cadenceHaulHint: How long a colony is left to fill before you empty it. This sets the Launchpad and Storage each colony needs: a full Launchpad stops extraction dead, so it decides whether what you dug up ever arrives.

settings.title: Settings

faq.storeIntro: Neocom Desk keeps as little as possible on a server. The short version: we store the things you make in the app, and none of what we read from EVE on your behalf.

synced.title: Synced between your devices
synced.description: Saved so your work looks the same on your phone, your laptop and your desktop. Filed under each character’s EVE character ID — never a name, an email address, or an account we invented.
synced.skillPlans: Skill Plans — the plans you build. The skills you have actually trained come from EVE and stay on this device.
synced.buildPlans: Build Plans — the blueprint, runs, ME/TE, facility and hub you picked.
synced.productionRuns: Production Runs — what you logged as built, and the sales and orders you linked to it.
synced.quickbar: Your Quickbar — the items you saved in the Market browser.
synced.stationPins: The stations and structures you pinned in Assets.
synced.piPicks: The resources you chose to pull on each planet in the PI Advisor.
synced.miningTaxNote: The payees you named and the entries you assigned to them, including the ore and ISK figures snapshotted at that moment — that snapshot is the invoice, so it has to travel with it.
synced.notificationFeedNote: Ones you have already been shown, so another device can catch up on what it missed. Kept for 30 days.
synced.settings: The settings you chose on this page.
synced.settingsNote: Your notification preferences, the PI customs rates you overrode, your industry build groups, the defaults every page starts from — trade hub, industry facility, reaction facility, assumed ME and assumed TE, the PI expiring-soon window, the corp dark threshold, and the default characters shown — the appraisal price percentage you set on the Market page, whether SP Extraction monitoring is on along with the SP threshold you set for it, and whether blueprint cost counts toward Industry profit. Nothing else on this page leaves your device.

local.title: Kept on this device only
local.description: Everything Neocom Desk reads from EVE is cached in this browser and refetched from ESI when it goes stale. None of it is uploaded. The one thing Neocom Desk writes back to your account: opening a mail here marks it read in EVE too, so it stays read after you reload. Nothing else — no orders, no messages, no colony changes — is ever written.
local.esi: Your assets, wallet, contracts, mail, contacts, clones, calendar, skills, skill queue, industry jobs and colonies.
local.corp: Everything on the Corporation pages — wallet, members, structures, assets and moon extractions.
local.market: Market prices, order books and the LP store.
local.loginNote: The token that keeps you logged in is stored in this browser and nowhere else.
local.preferences: The rest of Settings — text size and time format, which answer for the screen you are looking at — and every sort, filter and expanded section a page remembers as you use it.

notes.push: Push notifications, if you turn them on: we store a token for this device, the character IDs it covers, and the alerts due in the next 72 hours — including their text, so they can be delivered while the app is closed. Each character is verified with EVE at that moment, and the token used for that check is discarded straight after.
notes.crashes: Crash reports: when something goes wrong we receive the error and which page it happened on, so it can be fixed. IP addresses are switched off, request and response bodies are never captured, and your EVE tokens are stripped before anything is sent.
notes.removal: Removing a character deletes everything above from our servers. If its EVE login has already expired we cannot sign in to do that, so the deletion runs the next time you add that character back.
notes.export: Exporting a backup (Data tab) writes a password-encrypted file — including your sign-in tokens — to your device. This only happens when you press the button, and the file goes wherever you choose to put it; we never see it.
